name: Hurricane Electric

profile.reading: Hurricane Electric Fremont 1 sits at 760 Mission Court, Fremont, California 94539, also the company's own stated corporate headquarters address. Hurricane Electric's own colocation page describes a 45,000 square foot facility with 1,000 cabinets, diverse UPS and generator backup power, 2 internet exchange points (SFMIX and FCIX), 6 carriers with diverse fiber, and connections to 20 internet networks, alongside individually locked cabinets, custom video surveillance, card keyed doors, raised floors, and 24 by 7 by 365 onsite staff and remote hands support. Hurricane Electric, per Wikipedia's own article, was established in 1994 by Mike Leber and operates under autonomous system number 6939, positioning itself as the largest global IP network by network adjacencies in both IPv4 and IPv6 as of June 2024, and the largest global IPv6 network by IPv6 prefixes announced. The company connects to more than 338 major exchange points, peers directly with more than 11,990 networks under an open peering policy requiring no contracts, and maintains more than 55 terabits per second of active public peering capacity and more than 900 terabits per second of private peering capacity. Hurricane Electric also operates a free IPv6 tunnel broker service that, as of June 2024, supported 52,760 provisioned tunnels across 174 countries. The company operates two other colocation facilities already on file elsewhere in this registry, a second Fremont building known as Fremont 2 and a smaller San Jose facility at 55 South Market Street. Fremont sits in the southern San Francisco Bay Area, in Alameda County, a secondary but well established Bay Area colocation and interconnection market that offers lower real estate and power costs than downtown San Francisco or San Jose while remaining close enough to Silicon Valley's dense fiber infrastructure for network operators like Hurricane Electric to maintain the low latency peering relationships central to its business model.

reading:
Hurricane Electric is a network operator that happens to own buildings, not a colocation platform that happens to run a network, and reading its registry entry any other way will produce the wrong numbers.

The American Registry for Internet Numbers records autonomous system 6939 as registered to Hurricane Electric LLC on 28 June 1996. PeeringDB, the interconnection registry that networks maintain about themselves, describes AS6939 as a global network service provider with an open peering policy, traffic in the 100 terabits per second and above band, roughly 210,000 IPv4 prefixes and 180,000 IPv6 prefixes in its published announcement counts, presence in 343 facilities worldwide and connections at 338 internet exchange points. Those are network density figures. They are not power figures and they are not comparable with the megawatt numbers recorded against wholesale operators elsewhere in this registry.

The company's own colocation page lists three sites, and the registry holds two of them. Fremont 2, at 48233 Warm Springs Boulevard, Fremont, California 94539, is described as 200,000 square feet with about 3,000 cabinets, with diverse A and B power that the company describes as fully separate power distribution units, panels, transformers and generators, and with 295 networks and 13 internet exchange points reachable inside the building across eight carriers. Fremont 1, at 760 Mission Court, Fremont 94539, is described as 45,000 square feet with about 1,000 cabinets on uninterruptible and generator backed power, with 20 networks and two exchange points across six carriers. The third site, Hurricane San Jose at 55 South Market Street, Suite 1400, is only about 3,000 square feet of racks in cages inside a shared CoreSite building, and its absence from the registry is defensible, since it is a tenancy in someone else's data centre rather than a Hurricane Electric facility.

760 Mission Court is also the corporate address the company prints on its own contact page, so the Fremont 1 row is both a data centre and the company head office.

What is not published anywhere is the power. Hurricane Electric states no IT load, no utility service size and no standby generator rating for either Fremont building. Square footage and cabinet counts are the only capacity numbers it puts in public, and there is no securities filing to check them against, because no company under this name appears as a registrant in the SEC EDGAR company index. The record for this operator is its own site and the internet number registries, and that is the whole of it.
